dimensions.assessment: Directly affects clinical psychologists participating in Medicare, facilities such as skilled nursing facilities, home health agencies, and rehabilitation centers, and Medicare beneficiaries in shortage areas.
dimensions.evidence: services furnished by a clinical psychologist... in an area that is designated... as a health professional shortage area

dimensions.assessment: Provides a moderate financial incentive (10 percent payment bonus) and administrative flexibility by aligning clinical psychologist service permissions with state laws across facilities.
dimensions.evidence: there also shall be paid to the clinical psychologist... an amount equal to 10 percent of the payment amount

dimensions.assessment: Involves additional payments made from the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund for services in shortage areas, though the total aggregate fiscal cost is not stated.
dimensions.evidence: there also shall be paid to the clinical psychologist... from the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund

dimensions.assessment: Amends Medicare provisions under Title XVIII of the Social Security Act regarding provider payment incentives and administrative oversight rules in multiple facility types.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to expand access to psychological and behavioral services.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent Medicare policy changes effective for services furnished on or after January 1, 2027.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this section shall apply to services furnished on or after January 1, 2027.

missing_information: Projected aggregate expenditure from the Federal Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund
importance_detail.rationale: The Increasing Mental Health Options Act of 2026 provides a 10 percent Medicare payment incentive for clinical psychologists practicing in health professional shortage areas and removes physician supervision or approval requirements for clinical psychologists in specified institutional care settings.
